title: CDC says no juice before 12 months, and at most 4 ounces of 100 percent juice from ages 1 to 3
summary: CDC says children younger than 12 months should not drink fruit or vegetable juice, and cites a 4-ounce cap after that.
body: The CDC page dated 14 April 2026 says children younger than 12 months should not drink any fruit or vegetable juice. It says juice after 12 months is unnecessary. It reports the American Academy of Pediatrics recommendation of no more than 4 ounces of 100 percent fruit juice a day for children ages 1 through 3 years. Fruit drinks, fruit-flavored drinks, and juice drinks have added sugars, and the page says children should not have them. The page suggests whole fruits instead. This is United States guidance as CDC prints it, including the Academy line it repeats. It is not a sippy-cup rule for the whole world.

sources.note: Supports the under-12-months ban and the 4-ounce sentence. Public-domain CDC page. Paraphrased.
